messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a pattern where a few bursty tenants are trashing the KV prefix cache and causing tail-sampled traces for other customers to be evicted. Noticed this on foxcorp during today's load test (p90 eviction latency spike).

aj: Ugh. Did you correlate with per-route QPS or bundle size?

maria: Yes, route QPS spikes on /generate-chat, and they have long-lived conversations so KV prefixes are big. Our current head/tail sampler is tenant-agnostic, LRU on prefix keyspace.

sasha: Can you paste the eviction metric?

maria: Metrics: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/rt-telemetry/kvcache — look at evictions/sec and prefix_kv_size_by_tenant. Also saw increased tail sampling drop-rate.

kevin: Hypothesis: heavy tenants should get tenant-aware head sampling quota + route-weighted tail sampling. That way we keep representative tails for small tenants.

tariq: Agree. Two knobs we might need: per-tenant head budget and a route priority multiplier (so payment-tier/customers with SLA get higher tail retention).

lucy: Edge case: what if a bursty tenant is also high priority? We can't give them unlimited head because they'd still evict others. Need eviction policy that accounts for tenant fairness.

aj: Proposal sketch:
1) per-tenant head cap: max_head_per_minute (default 200)
2) route multiplier: route_priority in {low,normal,high} -> multiplier {0.5,1,2}
3) eviction weight = prefix_size * tenant_load_factor / route_priority

maria: prototype config I tested locally:
```json
{
  "sampling": {
    "default_head_per_minute": 200,
    "per_tenant_caps": {"foxcorp": 600},
    "route_priority": {"/generate-chat": "high", "/embed": "normal"}
  }
}
```

sasha: Nice. What's the policy for tail sampling? Do we do deterministic tail per-tenant or reservoir sampling across tenants?

maria: I'm leaning reservoir per-tenant + global bucket for unexpected tails. That prevents small tenants from starving.

kevin: Also add an adaptive burst window: if tenant QPS > threshold, temporarily increase head cap but mark samples with tenant_burst=true metadata so downstream retention rules can treat them differently.

tariq: Need to think about disk/retention costs for tails. If we increase caps during bursts we must have a safety limiter that shifts older tails to short-retention storage.

ops-bot: @oncall: memory pressure alert on telemetry-kv-cache pod telemetry-cache-03 at 04:12 UTC — evictions spiked by 4x.

lucy: Ops alert confirms correlation. We should patch config in prod staging to enforce per-tenant caps then run canary.

maria: Plan: (1) implement tenant_head_cap and route_multiplier in sampling service, (2) add eviction_weight calc, (3) ship to staging with canary 10% traffic, (4) monitor evictions/trace-completeness for 24h.

aj: Can you add a small /sampling/config API so console can display and override caps for enterprise customers? UX folks want visibility.

maria: Yup — will add a read/write endpoint with audit log. Example response: "{ \"tenant\": \"foxcorp\", \"head_cap\": 600, \"route_mul\": {\"/generate-chat\":\"high\"} }"

kevin: Quick note on implementation: keep the sampler decision cheap (no global locks). Use local counters + occasional sync to control-plane. Don’t query DB on every request.

sasha: For tests, add synthetic tenant burst tests and measure tail coverage per-tenant. Also add perf test to ensure sampler adds <200ns p99 to request path.

tariq: I'll take ownership of canary run and dashboard panels. We'll need panels: tenant_evictions, prefix_kv_size_by_tenant, tail_sampled_rate_by_tenant, sampled_trace_retention_by_tier.

maria: Thanks — I'll open a short PR with config and unit tests. Posting draft CL in a bit. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment queued for telemetry-sampler branch feature/tenant-head-cap to staging (canary=10%). Expected rollout 5m.

aj: After canary, we should evaluate whether to add a soft quota feedback to clients (429-esque metric) so SDKs can back off short-lived bursts. Maybe not now.

lucy: FYI: PM asked for a brief note for console team so they can show current sampling state to enterprise customers. I'll loop them in.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/p/r/1234 — comments welcome. I'll schedule follow-up sync tomorrow to review metrics after canary.

sasha: Thanks — nice approach. Low-risk incremental rollout sounds good.

kevin: If it looks stable, consider adding an opt-in higher head budget for Dedicated customers via billing tier.

maria: noted. Closing loop after canary results.
